options: Hundreds of flat, unstructured workspaces created ad hoc with no organizing principle
A tenant setting that limits the number of workspaces a user can create
A single workspace that has grown too large in storage size
The automatic archiving of unused workspaces after 90 days
questions.explain: Workspace sprawl describes an unstructured proliferation of workspaces with no naming convention or organizing principle, making discovery and ownership nearly impossible.

questions.q: What are the three ways a workspace can be assigned to a domain?
options: Only by manually dragging workspaces in the admin portal
By workspace name, by workspace admin, or by capacity
By report type, by refresh schedule, or by data source
By tenant setting, by sensitivity label, or by RLS role
questions.explain: The 'Assign workspaces to this domain' pane offers three methods: assign by workspace name, by workspace admin, or by capacity.

questions.q: Why is assigning workspaces to a domain 'by capacity' especially useful at scale?
options: It automatically applies row-level security to every workspace in the capacity
It permanently locks the domain assignment and prevents future changes
If dev/test/prod each run on dedicated capacities, it moves every workspace on that capacity into the domain in one action
It's the only method that works for workspaces outside Premium capacity
questions.explain: Assigning by capacity lets an admin move potentially dozens of workspaces into a domain in a single action, rather than selecting them individually by name or admin.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's wrong with storing production content in 'My workspace'?
options: My workspace cannot contain semantic models, only reports
My workspace content is automatically deleted after 30 days
A personal workspace has no shared access model, so content can become orphaned if that person leaves
There is nothing wrong with it — it's the recommended pattern for production content
questions.explain: My workspace is personal and has no role-based access model shared with a team, so production content placed there is at risk if the owner leaves the organization.

questions.q: What naming convention does this lesson recommend for workspace names?
options: [Team]-[Project]-[Environment], e.g. Finance-Budgeting-Prod
A random alphanumeric ID assigned automatically by Power BI
Generic names like 'Reports' or 'Test' for simplicity
The workspace creator's own name only
questions.explain: A Team-Project-Environment pattern (e.g. Finance-Budgeting-Prod) is sortable, searchable, and self-documenting — generic names like 'Reports' or 'Test' become meaningless over time.
